origins.section: A Class Is Loaded When Code First Needs It, and Initialised Only When Code First Uses It
Each Loader Asks Its Parent First, So the JDK's Classes Always Come from the JDK's Loaders
Static Initialisers Run in Textual Order, and a Cycle Lets Code Read a Field Before It Is Set
Two Threads That Initialise a Cycle from Both Ends Wait for Each Other Forever

recorded.outcome:q-legacy-exporter-banner: Lines 72-80: 'PdfRenderer was loaded before main printed anything, yet its static block never ran' (args empty, so the PdfRenderer branch never ran); 'Initialisation ... waits for the first new, call of a static method ..., or read or write of a static field that isn't a compile-time constant'. The output (lines 62-69) shows a load line for PdfRenderer and no 'init PdfRenderer'. The quiz's setup matches: an abstract class with the unused subclass on one branch.

recorded.outcome:q-fixture-loader: Lines 114-117: 'ClassLoader.loadClass first returns one this loader has already loaded, then asks its parent, and only when the parent fails calls its own findClass'. Lines 191-193 and 203-207: with the app loader as parent, Exporter (also in the plugin dir) is 'defined by app', 'The copy in the plugin directory is never read', and getClassLoader() reports the defining loader.
recorded.prompt:q-free-plan-limits: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-free-plan-limits: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-free-plan-limits: Lines 240-244: static fields start at their defaults; initialisers run top to bottom; a same-thread read during initialisation 'returns the field's default, 0'. Lines 250-252: a compile-time constant is copied into the reading class by javac ('bipush 20') and 'reading it initialises nothing'. So MAX_SEATS=5 is inlined, and MAX_PROJECTS (Integer.getInteger, not a constant, declared after FREE) reads 0.

Lines 290-300: the thread dump shows 'waiting on the Class initialization monitor'.

recorded.pass:q-fixture-loader:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-fixture-loader:b: Lines 205-207: 'The plugin loader is the initiating loader of that Exporter, the application loader its defining loader, and getClassLoader() reports the defining one.' The loader that was asked is not necessarily the one that defines the class.
recorded.prompt:q-fixture-loader:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-fixture-loader:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-fixture-loader:c: Lines 187-190 and 197-200: with the platform loader as parent, the plugin loader defines its own Exporter even though Exporter is on the app class path (the cast message says the host's is 'loader app'). So whether the app loader defines a class depends on delegation, not on the class being on the class path. The Design Note (lines 417-421) on child-first loading points the same way. PARTLY TRUE: the answer it names (the application loader) is correct; only the reason is wrong.

recorded.outcome:q-fixture-loader:d: Lines 114-117 describe parent-first for every class, with no restriction to a package. Lines 203-205: the plugin loader passes its request for the non-java Exporter up to the application loader.

recorded.outcome:q-startup-hang-agent:b: Lines 273-287: threads that are waiting on each other's class initialisation lock report state=RUNNABLE on Java 21, so RUNNABLE doesn't show that they are working. The opening (line 4) also gives an idle CPU.
recorded.prompt:q-startup-hang-agent:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-startup-hang-agent:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-startup-hang-agent:c: The heading on line 257 says 'Wait for Each Other Forever'. Line 304: 'Every later thread that touches either class joins the wait.' Lines 286-287: the check misses the deadlock because 'it tracks only monitors and java.util.concurrent locks', not because of when it runs.
recorded.prompt:q-startup-hang-agent:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-startup-hang-agent:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-startup-hang-agent:d: Line 281 and lines 285-287: for two threads that do wait for each other (in class initialisation), findDeadlockedThreads returns null. Its silence therefore doesn't show that no thread is waiting.
